name: Dixon Power Systems
old_description: After 17 years of owning an automotive repair shop, Jon Dixon needed a new challenge and had a growing interest in Renewable Energy. With the encouragement of his wife Holly, the business was launched. Dixon Power Systems began as a part-time business in the spring of 1999 and expanded to full time in January of 2005.
about:
Dixon Power Systems is based in Lincoln, Nebraska. The company traces its roots to 1999 when Jon Dixon, after 17 years running an automotive repair shop, launched a part-time venture in renewable energy with encouragement from his wife Holly. The operation became full-time in January 2005. The business remains a privately held, husband-and-wife enterprise.

The firm designs and installs custom solar photovoltaic and wind turbine systems for on-grid, off-grid, and backup-power applications. It also operates a storefront where customers can purchase pre-engineered system packages and components. Services include site assessment, system engineering, procurement, installation, and commissioning. No facility size or headcount figures are publicly disclosed.

Clients range from homeowners and farms to small businesses seeking independence from utility power or reliable backup electricity. Typical projects serve customers in remote locations without grid access, those pursuing environmental goals, and others wanting resilience against outages. The company has supplied systems for residential, agricultural, and light-commercial installations across Nebraska and neighboring states.

Jon Dixon’s background in automotive mechanical and electrical systems informed the company’s hands-on, problem-solving approach. He has pursued continuing education with industry experts and serves on the board of Nebraskans for Solar. The founders frame their mission around energy independence, emphasizing user-friendly designs that address each site’s unique constraints.
